sanskrit: te yattā bhīmasenena sahitāḥ kāñcanadhvajāḥ pratyadṛśyanta rājendra sendrā iva divaukasaḥ
english: Vigilant and arrayed with Bhīmasena, their golden banners aloft, they appeared, O lord of kings, like the dwellers of heaven with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: atyarocata tān sarvān dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ samāgatān sarvāṇy api ca sainyāni bhāradvājo 'tyarocata
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna outshone all those gathered warriors; yet over all the armies, the son of Bharadvāja shone more brilliantly still.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca vyathayeyur ime senāṃ devānām api saṃyuge āhave ye nyavartanta vṛkodaramukhā rathāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: These chariot-warriors, with Vṛkodara at their head, who wheeled back into the fray, could shake even the host of the gods in battle.

sanskrit: saṃprayuktaḥ kilaivāyaṃ diṣṭair bhavati pūruṣaḥ tasminn eva tu sarvārthā dṛśyante vai pṛthagvidhāḥ
english: A man, it seems, is yoked fast to his fate; and within that fate alone are all his manifold ends seen to lie.

sanskrit: dīrghaṃ viproṣitaḥ kālam araṇye jaṭilo 'jinī ajñātaś caiva lokasya vijahāra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: For a long span Yudhiṣṭhira dwelt exiled in the forest, his hair matted, clad in deerskin, and wandered unknown to the world.

sanskrit: sa eva mahatīṃ senāṃ samāvartayad āhave kim anyad daivasaṃyogān mama putrasya cābhavat
english: That very man has now marshalled a mighty army for battle. What was this, if not the working of destiny, that has befallen my son?

sanskrit: yukta eva hi bhāgyena dhruvam utpadyate naraḥ sa tathākṛṣyate tena na yathā svayam icchati
english: Surely a man is born already bound to his lot, and is dragged along by it, not as he himself would wish.

sanskrit: dyūtavyasanam āsādya kleśito hi yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sa punar bhāgadheyena sahāyān upalabdhavān
english: Having fallen into the calamity of the dice, Yudhiṣṭhira was sorely afflicted; yet again, by his appointed fortune, he has gained allies.

sanskrit: ardhaṃ me kekayā labdhāḥ kāśikāḥ kosalāś ca ye cedayaś cāpare vaṅgā mām eva samupāśritāḥ
english: Half the Kekayas have fallen to me, and the Kāśis, the Kosalas, the Cedis, and besides them the Vaṅgas have leaned upon me alone.

sanskrit: pṛthivī bhūyasī tāta mama pārthasya no tathā iti mām abravīt sūta mando duryodhanas tadā
english: "Mine is the greater part of the earth, dear sire, not so the son of Pṛthā's" — thus, O sūta, did foolish Duryodhana speak to me then.

sanskrit: tasya senāsamūhasya madhye droṇaḥ surakṣitaḥ nihataḥ pārṣatenājau kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: In the midst of that gathered host Droṇa was well guarded, yet he has been slain in the field by the son of Pṛṣata. What was this, if not the work of fate?

sanskrit: madhye rājñāṃ mahābāhuṃ sadā yuddhābhinandinam sarvāstrapāragaṃ droṇaṃ kathaṃ mṛtyur upeyivān
english: How did death come upon Droṇa — the mighty-armed, ever rejoicing in battle, master of every weapon — there in the very midst of kings?

sanskrit: samanuprāptakṛcchro 'haṃ saṃmohaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ bhīṣmadroṇau hatau śrutvā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: Overtaken by anguish, I have sunk into utter bewilderment; hearing that both Bhīṣma and Droṇa are slain, I have no heart to live.

sanskrit: yan mā kṣattābravīt tāta prapaśyan putragṛddhinam duryodhanena tat sarvaṃ prāptaṃ sūta mayā saha
english: All that Vidura, seeing me greedy for my sons' sake, foretold to me, dear sire — all that, O sūta, has now come to pass for Duryodhana along with me.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaṃ tu paraṃ tat syāt tyaktvā duryodhanaṃ yadi putraśeṣaṃ cikīrṣeyaṃ kṛcchraṃ na maraṇaṃ bhavet
english: Yet it would be the height of cruelty if, forsaking Duryodhana, I should seek to preserve my remaining sons; only hardship, and not death, would follow.

sanskrit: yo hi dharmaṃ parityajya bhavaty arthaparo naraḥ so 'smāc ca hīyate lokāt kṣudrabhāvaṃ ca gacchati
english: For the man who forsakes righteousness and becomes devoted to gain falls away from this world too, and sinks into baseness.

sanskrit: adya cāpy asya rāṣṭrasya hatotsāhasya saṃjaya avaśeṣaṃ na paśyāmi kakude mṛdite sati
english: And now too, Saṃjaya, of this kingdom whose spirit is broken, I see no remnant left, its very hump crushed in.

sanskrit: kathaṃ syād avaśeṣaṃ hi dhuryayor abhyatītayoḥ yau nityam anujīvāmaḥ kṣamiṇau puruṣarṣabhau
english: How can anything remain when the two draught-bulls have passed away — those two forbearing bulls among men, upon whom we forever lived?

sanskrit: vyaktam eva ca me śaṃsa yathā yuddham avartata ke 'yudhyan ke vyapākarṣan ke kṣudrāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: Tell me plainly how the battle unfolded: who fought, who drew back, and which base men fled in fear.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaṃ ca me śaṃsa yad yac cakre ratharṣabhaḥ tasmād bhayaṃ no bhūyiṣṭhaṃ bhrātṛvyāc ca viśeṣataḥ
english: And tell me of Dhanaṃjaya, all that the bull among chariot-warriors did; for from him is our greatest fear, and from that foeman-cousin above all.

sanskrit: yathāsīc ca nivṛtteṣu pāṇḍaveṣu ca saṃjaya mama sainyāvaśeṣasya saṃnipātaḥ sudāruṇaḥ māmakānāṃ ca ye śūrāḥ kāṃs tatra samavārayan
english: And when the Pāṇḍavas had wheeled about, Saṃjaya, how did the dreadful clash of what remained of my army come to be, and which of my heroes held off which foes there?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca mahad bhairavam āsīn naḥ saṃnivṛtteṣu pāṇḍuṣu dṛṣṭvā droṇaṃ chādyamānaṃ tair bhāskaram ivāmbudaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: A great terror seized us when the Pāṇḍavas had wheeled about, beholding Droṇa overspread by them as the sun by storm-clouds.

sanskrit: taiś coddhūtaṃ rajas tīvram avacakre camūṃ tava tato hatam amanyāma droṇaṃ dṛṣṭipathe hate
english: The fierce dust they raised wrapped your host in darkness, and when the line of sight was lost we believed Droṇa already slain.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu śūrān maheṣvāsān krūraṃ karma cikīrṣataḥ dṛṣṭvā duryodhanas tūrṇaṃ svasainyaṃ samacūcudat
english: But seeing those heroes, great archers bent on a cruel deed, Duryodhana swiftly urged on his own troops.

sanskrit: yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ yathāsattvaṃ narādhipāḥ vārayadhvaṃ yathāyogaṃ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: "To the utmost of your strength, your zeal, and your mettle, O kings, hold back as best you can the army of the Pāṇḍavas!"

sanskrit: tato durmarṣaṇo bhīmam abhyagacchat sutas tava ārād dṛṣṭvā kiran bāṇair icchan droṇasya jīvitam
english: Then your son Durmarṣaṇa, seeing Bhīma from afar, advanced upon him, scattering arrows, longing to preserve Droṇa's life.

sanskrit: taṃ bāṇair avatastāra kruddho mṛtyum ivāhave taṃ ca bhīmo 'tudad bāṇais tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: Enraged, he covered Bhīma with shafts, like Death himself in battle; and Bhīma struck back at him with arrows, and a great tumult arose.

sanskrit: ta īśvarasamādiṣṭāḥ prājñāḥ śūrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ bāhyaṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ kṛtvā pratyatiṣṭhan parān yudhi
english: Those wise and valiant strikers, commanded by their lord, set aside all fear of death and stood firm against their foes in the fight.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā śineḥ putraṃ droṇaprepsuṃ viśāṃ pate paryavārayad āyāntaṃ śūraṃ samitiśobhanam
english: Kṛtavarman, O lord of peoples, beset the grandson of Śini as he came on — that hero, ornament of the assembly, eager to reach Droṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ śaineyaḥ śaravrātaiḥ kruddhaḥ kruddham avārayat kṛtavarmā ca śaineyaṃ matto mattam iva dvipam
english: The grandson of Śini, enraged, held off the enraged Kṛtavarman with showers of shafts, and Kṛtavarman held off the grandson of Śini, as one rutting elephant another.

sanskrit: saindhavaḥ kṣatradharmāṇam āpatantaṃ śaraughiṇam ugradhanvā maheṣvāsaṃ yatto droṇād avārayat
english: The Saindhava, fierce of bow and a great archer, with effort held back from Droṇa the onrushing Kṣatradharman, that wielder of arrow-floods.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmā sindhupateś chittvā ketanakārmuke nārācair bahubhiḥ kruddhaḥ sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: Kṣatradharman, having shorn away the banner and bow of the lord of the Sindhus, struck him in wrath with many iron shafts in all his vital parts.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya saindhavaḥ kṛtahastavat vivyādha kṣatradharmāṇaṃ raṇe sarvāyasaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the Saindhava, deft of hand, pierced Kṣatradharman in the field with shafts wholly of iron.

sanskrit: yuyutsuṃ pāṇḍavārthāya yatamānaṃ mahāratham subāhur bhrātaraṃ śūraṃ yatto droṇād avārayat
english: Subāhu, with effort, held off from Droṇa his own brother — the great chariot-warrior Yuyutsu, that hero who strove for the Pāṇḍavas' cause.

sanskrit: subāhoḥ sadhanurbāṇāv asyataḥ parighopamau yuyutsuḥ śitapītābhyāṃ kṣurābhyām acchinad bhujau
english: As Subāhu, mace-like of arm, loosed his arrows, Yuyutsu severed both his arms, bow and shaft and all, with two whetted, gold-bright razor-shafts.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram veleva sāgaraṃ kṣubdhaṃ madrarāṭ samavārayat
english: The king of the Madras held back King Yudhiṣṭhira, best of the Pāṇḍavas, the righteous-souled, as a shore holds back the heaving sea.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmarājo bahubhir marmabhidbhir avākirat madreśas taṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā śarair viddhvānadad bhṛśam
english: The King of Righteousness covered him with many vital-piercing shafts, and the lord of the Madras, having pierced him with sixty-four arrows, roared aloud.

sanskrit: tasya nānadataḥ ketum uccakarta sakārmukam kṣurābhyāṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhas tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: As the Madra king roared, the best of the Pāṇḍavas struck off his banner together with his bow by two razor-shafts, and at that the people raised a shout.

sanskrit: tathaiva rājā bāhlīko rājānaṃ drupadaṃ śaraiḥ ādravantaṃ sahānīkaṃ sahānīko nyavārayat
english: Even so King Bāhlika, with his own host, held off with his shafts King Drupada, who came charging on with his host.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ vṛddhayoḥ sahasenayoḥ yathā mahāyūthapayor dvipayoḥ saṃprabhinnayoḥ
english: Terrible grew the battle of those two aged kings with their armies, like that of two great herd-leading elephants, both in rut.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau virāṭaṃ matsyam ārcchatām sahasainyau sahānīkaṃ yathendrāgnī purā balim
english: The two Avanti princes, Vinda and Anuvinda, with their troops, fell upon Virāṭa the Matsya king and his host, as of old Indra and Agni fell upon Bali.

sanskrit: tad utpiñjalakaṃ yuddham āsīd devāsuropamam matsyānāṃ kekayaiḥ sārdham abhītāśvarathadvipam
english: A churning, confused fight arose, like that of gods and demons, between the Matsyas and the Kekayas, with horse and chariot and elephant unafraid.

sanskrit: nākuliṃ tu śatānīkaṃ bhūtakarmā sabhāpatiḥ asyantam iṣujālāni yāntaṃ droṇād avārayat
english: Bhūtakarman, lord of the assembly, held back from Droṇa the son of Nakula, Śatānīka, as he came on loosing nets of arrows.

sanskrit: tato nakuladāyādas tribhir bhallaiḥ susaṃśitaiḥ cakre vibāhuśirasaṃ bhūtakarmāṇam āhave
english: Then the heir of Nakula, with three keenly whetted broad-headed shafts, made Bhūtakarman armless and headless in the fray.

sanskrit: sutasomaṃ tu vikrāntam āpatantaṃ śaraughiṇam droṇāyābhimukhaṃ vīraṃ viviṃśatir avārayat
english: Viviṃśati held back the valiant Sutasoma, that hero, as he rushed on with floods of arrows, his face set toward Droṇa.

sanskrit: sutasomas tu saṃkruddhaḥ svapitṛvyam ajihmagaiḥ viviṃśatiṃ śarair viddhvā nābhyavartata daṃśitaḥ
english: But Sutasoma, in great wrath, having pierced his own uncle Viviṃśati with straight-flying shafts, did not turn back, armoured as he was.

sanskrit: atha bhīmarathaḥ śālvam āśugair āyasaiḥ śitaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ sāśvaniyantāram anayad yamasādanam
english: Then Bhīmaratha, with six swift, whetted iron shafts, sent Śālva, together with his horses and driver, to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: śrutakarmāṇam āyāntaṃ mayūrasadṛśair hayaiḥ caitrasenir mahārāja tava pautro nyavārayat
english: Śrutakarman, who came on with peacock-hued horses, was held back, O great king, by the son of Citrasena, your grandson.

sanskrit: tau pautrau tava durdharṣau parasparavadhaiṣiṇau pitṝṇām arthasiddhyarthaṃ cakratur yuddham uttamam
english: Those two unassailable grandsons of yours, each seeking the other's death, waged a surpassing combat for the sake of their fathers' cause.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhantam agrato dṛṣṭvā prativindhyaṃ tam āhave drauṇir mānaṃ pituḥ kurvan mārgaṇaiḥ samavārayat
english: Seeing Prativindhya standing before him in the field, the son of Droṇa, doing honour to his father, held him back with his arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ kruddhaḥ prativivyādha prativindhyaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ siṃhalāṅgūlalakṣmāṇaṃ pitur arthe vyavasthitam
english: In wrath Prativindhya pierced him back with whetted shafts — him whose ensign bore the lion's tail, who stood there for his father's sake.

sanskrit: pravapann iva bījāni bījakāle nararṣabha drauṇāyanir draupadeyaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: As one scattering seed in the sowing-season, O bull among men, the son of Droṇa covered the son of Draupadī with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: yas tu śūratamo rājan senayor ubhayor mataḥ taṃ paṭaccarahantāraṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ samavārayat
english: He who was held the most valiant, O king, in both armies — that slayer of the Paṭaccaras — Lakṣmaṇa held back.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇasyeṣvasanaṃ chittvā lakṣma ca bhārata lakṣmaṇe śarajālāni visṛjan bahv aśobhata
english: He, having severed Lakṣmaṇa's bow and his ensign, O Bhārata, loosing nets of arrows upon Lakṣmaṇa, shone forth exceedingly.

sanskrit: vikarṇas tu mahāprājño yājñaseniṃ śikhaṇḍinam paryavārayad āyāntaṃ yuvānaṃ samare yuvā
english: Vikarṇa, deeply wise, a youth himself, beset the young Śikhaṇḍin, son of Yajñasena, as he came on into the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tam iṣujālena yājñaseniḥ samāvṛṇot vidhūya tad bāṇajālaṃ babhau tava suto balī
english: Then the son of Yajñasena enveloped him in a net of arrows; but your mighty son, shaking off that net of shafts, shone forth.

sanskrit: aṅgado 'bhimukhaḥ śūram uttamaujasam āhave droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ vatsadantair avārayat
english: Aṅgada, turning to face the hero Uttamaujas in battle as he advanced toward Droṇa, held him back with calf-tooth shafts.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulas tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ sainikānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tayoś ca prītivardhanaḥ
english: That tumultuous clash of those two lions among men heightened the delight of all the soldiers, and of the two themselves as well.

sanskrit: durmukhas tu maheṣvāso vīraṃ purujitaṃ balī droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ kuntibhojam avārayat
english: And the mighty Durmukha, a great archer, held back the hero Purujit Kuntibhoja as he advanced toward Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa durmukhaṃ bhruvor madhye nārācena vyatāḍayat tasya tad vibabhau vaktraṃ sanālam iva paṅkajam
english: He struck Durmukha with an iron shaft between the brows, and that face of his shone like a lotus upon its stalk.

sanskrit: karṇas tu kekayān bhrātṝn pañca lohitakadhvajān droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yātāñ śaravarṣair avārayat
english: And Karṇa held back with showers of shafts the five Kekaya brothers, their banners crimson, as they advanced toward Droṇa.

sanskrit: te cainaṃ bhṛśasaṃkruddhāḥ śaravrātair avākiran sa ca tāṃś chādayām āsa śarajālaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: And they, in great wrath, covered him with masses of shafts, and he in turn overspread them again and again with nets of arrows.

sanskrit: naiva karṇo na te pañca dadṛśur bāṇasaṃvṛtāḥ sāśvasūtadhvajarathāḥ parasparaśarācitāḥ
english: Neither Karṇa nor those five could be seen, so wrapped were they in arrows — horses, drivers, banners, and chariots all studded with one another's shafts.

sanskrit: putras te durjayaś caiva jayaś ca vijayaś ca ha nīlaṃ kāśyaṃ jayaṃ śūrās trayas trīn pratyavārayan
english: Your sons Durjaya, Jaya, and Vijaya — those three heroes — held off in turn the three: Nīla, the Kāśi prince, and Jaya.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoram īkṣitṛprītivardhanam siṃhavyāghratarakṣūṇāṃ yathebhamahiṣarṣabhaiḥ
english: Terrible grew that battle, heightening the delight of those who watched, as of lions, tigers, and hyenas with elephants, buffaloes, and bulls.

sanskrit: kṣemadhūrtibṛhantau tau bhrātarau sātvataṃ yudhi droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ śarais tīkṣṇais tatakṣatuḥ
english: The two brothers Kṣemadhūrti and Bṛhanta hewed at the Sātvata in the fight with sharp shafts as he advanced toward Droṇa.

sanskrit: tayos tasya ca tad yuddham atyadbhutam ivābhavat siṃhasya dvipamukhyābhyāṃ prabhinnābhyāṃ yathā vane
english: The combat of those two and of him became wondrous indeed, like that of a lion with two lordly elephants in rut in the forest.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ tu tathāmbaṣṭham ekaṃ yuddhābhinandinam cedirājaḥ śarān asyan kruddho droṇād avārayat
english: And the king of the Cedis, loosing his shafts in wrath, held off from Droṇa the king of the Ambaṣṭhas, who alone rejoiced in battle.

sanskrit: tam ambaṣṭho 'sthibhedinyā niravidhyac chalākayā sa tyaktvā saśaraṃ cāpaṃ rathād bhūmim athāpatat
english: The Ambaṣṭha pierced him through with a bone-cleaving dart, and he, letting go bow and arrow, fell from his chariot to the ground.

sanskrit: vārdhakṣemiṃ tu vārṣṇeyaṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvataḥ śaraiḥ akṣudraḥ kṣudrakair droṇāt kruddharūpam avārayat
english: Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, no mean warrior, with small arrows held off from Droṇa the wrathful-seeming Vārdhakṣemi of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: yudhyantau kṛpavārṣṇeyau ye 'paśyaṃś citrayodhinau te yuddhasaktamanaso nānyā bubudhire kriyāḥ
english: Those who watched Kṛpa and the Vṛṣṇi fighting, brilliant in combat, became so engrossed in the battle that they marked no other doings.

sanskrit: saumadattis tu rājānaṃ maṇimantam atandritam paryavārayad āyāntaṃ yaśo droṇasya vardhayan
english: The son of Somadatta beset King Maṇimat, the unwearied, as he came on, thus increasing Droṇa's glory.

sanskrit: sa saumadattes tvaritaś chittveṣvasanaketane punaḥ patākāṃ sūtaṃ ca chatraṃ cāpātayad rathāt
english: He, swiftly cutting away the son of Somadatta's bow and banner, then cast down his pennon, his driver, and his parasol from the chariot.

sanskrit: athāplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ yūpaketur amitrahā sāśvasūtadhvajarathaṃ taṃ cakarta varāsinā
english: Then the foe-slayer whose ensign was the sacrificial post, leaping swiftly from his chariot, cut him to pieces — horses, driver, banner, and car — with his excellent sword.

sanskrit: rathaṃ ca svaṃ samāsthāya dhanur ādāya cāparam svayaṃ yacchan hayān rājan vyadhamat pāṇḍavīṃ camūm
english: And mounting his own chariot, taking up another bow, himself reining his horses, O king, he shattered the army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: musalair mudgaraiś cakrair bhiṇḍipālaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ pāṃsuvātāgnisalilair bhasmaloṣṭhatṛṇadrumaiḥ
english: With pestles, mallets, discs, slings, and battle-axes, with dust and wind and fire and water, with ashes, clods, grass, and trees —

sanskrit: ārujan prarujan bhañjan nighnan vidrāvayan kṣipan senāṃ vibhīṣayann āyād droṇaprepsur ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: breaking, crushing, shattering, slaying, scattering, and hurling, terrifying the host, Ghaṭotkaca came on, eager to reach Droṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ tu nānāpraharaṇair nānāyuddhaviśeṣaṇaiḥ rākṣasaṃ rākṣasaḥ kruddhaḥ samājaghne hy alambusaḥ
english: But the rākṣasa Alambusa, in wrath, fell upon that rākṣasa with weapons of every kind and every variety of war-craft.

sanskrit: tayos tad abhavad yuddhaṃ rakṣogrāmaṇimukhyayoḥ tādṛg yādṛk purā vṛttaṃ śambarāmararājayoḥ
english: The battle of those two foremost chiefs of the rākṣasas became such as once befell of old between Śambara and the king of the gods.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvaṃdvaśatāny āsan rathavāraṇavājinām padātīnāṃ ca bhadraṃ te tava teṣāṃ ca saṃkulam
english: Thus there were hundreds of single combats of chariots, elephants, and horsemen — and of foot-soldiers too — a mêlée, blessings upon you, between your men and theirs.
